html:
The Tetlit Gwich'in, the "people of the head waters", are a Gwich'in people of the Peel River in the Northwest Territories of Canada. Their main community is Fort McPherson.

They hunted caribou of the Porcupine herd, moose and fur animals in the mountains and along the Peel. In 1840 the Hudson's Bay Company built a post on the river, and trade drew them to it. Their neighbours were other Gwich'in to the west, the Inuvialuit on the coast and other Athabaskan groups up the Mackenzie. In 1992 the Gwich'in signed a land claim agreement with Canada.
